description: Frame-codec round-trip obligation for the `msgpack` CROSS-LANGUAGE BINARY DEFAULT (protocol.md § Frame codecs, #lzmsgpackparity). msgpack is a MUST for every binding and is implemented by two of nine; the other seven declare it as an explicit `carve_out` in their interop-peer handshake. That carve-out is honest and fails closed, but it was invisible to every parity surface: coverage.json had no codec row, and the four conformance rungs all reason about fixture CONTENT replay rather than codec round-tripping. This fixture is the msgpack half of the executable obligation, and a binding that does not implement msgpack now has to say so in its `KNOWN_UNCOVERED` ledger — the same place every other declared gap lives. The `wire` values are byte-identical to frame_roundtrip_json.json: the fixture pins the DECODED VALUE, never a golden byte string, because a MessagePack map's key order is encoder-defined and two conforming bindings MAY emit byte-different frames for the same IpcMessage (§ Frame codecs, 'Conformance is semantic round-trip, not byte-identical, for the map codecs'). A runner MUST decode `wire` from the reference json form, ENCODE it to msgpack bytes, DECODE those bytes back, and evaluate every `expect` key against that decode.

assertions.note: `byte_canonical: false` is the whole reason this fixture pins decoded values instead of golden bytes. msgpack frames encode each struct as a MessagePack MAP KEYED BY THE JSON FIELD NAME (Rust: `rmp_serde::to_vec_named`), not as a positional array — that is what keeps the omit-when-absent rule for the optional `key` uniform across json and msgpack, and it is what `encoded_body_field_names` below verifies. A positional encoder passes a naive value round trip and fails those keys.

scenarios.name: snapshot_frame_round_trips_msgpack
scenarios.description: The `Snapshot` variant survives a msgpack round trip, and the encoded frame is a named-field map. `encoded_envelope_key` pins the externally-tagged variant name at the top level; `encoded_body_field_names` (SORTED — msgpack map key order is encoder-defined, so a runner MUST sort before comparing) pins the named-field encoding. A positional array encoder round-trips fine and fails both. `first_node_encoded_field_names` carries NO `key`: `NodeSnapshot.key` is optional and a SELF-DESCRIBING codec omits it when absent (protocol.md § NodeKey), which is the rule that lets a pre-`key` decoder read a post-`key` frame. That the rule holds under msgpack exactly as under json is the whole point of named-field encoding.

scenarios.name: delta_frame_round_trips_msgpack
scenarios.description: The `Delta` variant survives a msgpack round trip across all seven DeltaOp variants, with the op envelope still externally tagged and the op body still a named-field map.

scenarios.name: crdt_sync_frame_round_trips_msgpack
scenarios.description: The `CrdtSync` variant survives a msgpack round trip with its frontier stamps and its keyed/keyless op split intact. `CrdtOp` differs from `NodeSnapshot` here and the difference is deliberate: a `CrdtOp` ALWAYS carries `key` (null when unset, as distributed/crdt_sync_frames.json states), because an anti-entropy op's addressing is part of the merge identity, whereas an absent `NodeSnapshot.key` is omitted. Both encoded field-name lists therefore carry `key`, and `first_op_key_absent` is asserted on the DECODED value, not on the encoding. Lists are sorted; msgpack map key order is encoder-defined.
